summary: LASER (Localized Area Seismicity Earth Radar) is a real-time environmental monitoring and early-warning web application designed to bridge open-source satellite data with local disaster prevention in high-risk seismic zones, such as the Mesa de los Santos in Santander, Colombia. Developed entirely in Python and deployed via Streamlit Community Cloud, LASER operates like an economic market broker for Earth's stability: it tracks daily surface variables from NASA POWER (temperature, GPM IMERG precipitation, and GLDAS soil moisture), combines them with live seismic feeds from the USGS, and evaluates terrain anomalies using a directional p-Index. The platform transforms complex telemetry into 4 actionable dashboard KPIs (thermal trends, p-index variations, soil saturation, and multi-hazard risk correlated with DANE population data). By identifying critical saturation thresholds before or after seismic events, LASER mitigates secondary cascading hazards like landslides and floods, empowering vulnerable communities with clear, data-driven early warnings.
details:
What it does & How it works:

LASER functions as an interactive command center structured into three core modules: (1) Command Center, featuring dynamic top metric cards (Thermal Trends via Mann-Kendall, p-Index directional anomaly tracking, GLDAS soil moisture, and cascading risk)alongside a real-time NASA GIBS and USGS seismic map; (2) Golden Window (72h), displaying short-term critical accumulation telemetry including 72h accumulated rainfall, maximum soil saturation, and thermal differentials; and (3) Seismic & Citizen Alert System, integrating live USGS FSDS data (3.5) with distance calculations to nodes and a real-time DANE population geocoding engine for precise risk assessment.

Scientific Methodology & Tools:

Developed using Python within Streamlit Community Cloud, the platform processes multi-source open datasets:

  • NASA POWER & GPM IMERG: Daily surface meteorology, temperature, and high-resolution precipitation tracking.
  • GLDAS (NASA): Soil moisture assimilation models used to calculate critical land saturation limits ($\ge 0.72$ threshold for landslide warnings).
  • USGS Earthquake Hazards API: Real-time seismic event tracking and epicentral distance analysis.
  • Statistical Engine: Non-parametric Mann-Kendall tests for long-term trend significance (p-values) and a directional p-Index using standard deviation control limits (1.8) to flag abrupt environmental irregularities.
dataRefs: NASA GLDAS – Global Land Data Assimilation System
NASA GIBS – Global Imagery Browse Services
ASF Vertex – NASA Alaska Satellite Facility DAAC (InSAR / Sentinel-1)
